$comment: i18n-lint's configuration. Stage1-AppShell-Plan.md 5.6 owns the rule set; this file is its
executable form. Adding a sink as ui/ grows should be a one-line diff with a reason in the
commit message, not a recompile of a gate.
THE SINK LIST IS THE RULE. 'A string literal that reaches a user' cannot be decided from the
literal alone -- object names, settings paths, catalog keys, format specifiers and log text are
all literals, and a rule that fires on those is a rule that gets waived everywhere and then
switched off. So the gate looks for the calls that put text in front of a person, and reports a
literal that reaches one of them unwrapped. The cost is a false negative for a literal handed
to a user through a helper this list does not name -- which is why the list is data and why it
is the first thing to check when a stray English string shows up in a zh-TW screenshot.
$comment-extensions: `.def` was added at T9 and is not a stylistic inclusion. This project keeps its permanent
public names in X-macro tables -- ActionId.def, SettingsKeys.def, KeyBindingDefaults.def and
now ui/shell/ShellKeys.def -- so the catalog key for a shell string is written in a .def and
nowhere else. Without this line every one of those keys is an `orphan-key` note on every run:
reported rather than failed (S3), and therefore a report that would slowly train people to
skip the whole orphan section. A .def is source; it is #included, not compiled, which is a
fact about the BUILD and not about whether a gate should read it.
`.json` was added at T10, and it is the same rule applied one step further out. res/ribbon.json
names 58 `ribbon.*` catalog keys -- every tab and group title in the product -- and it is the
single source of truth for them, because putting them in a .def as well would be two lists of
the same names. A gate reads the files that REFERENCE a key, and whether that file happens to be
compiled is a fact about the build rather than about what the gate is for (issue I-16).
$comment-keyFamilies: THE unknown-key RULE'S WHOLE INPUT, added at Stage 2 T16 -- issue I-04. Nothing here compared a
key a source REFERENCES against the catalogs: missing-key compares the shipped catalogs against
each other, action-label covers action.* from ActionId.def, and orphan-key is the INVERSE
question. So a key a source names and no catalog defines was invisible from both directions,
and eighteen of them shipped.
WHY A FAMILY LIST RATHER THAN 'EVERY DOTTED LITERAL'. The scanner's notion of a catalog key is
deliberately generous, because an over-broad reference set makes orphan-key QUIETER and
orphan-key is a note. unknown-key is the opposite: it BLOCKS, so the same generosity would
report settings.ini, pdfium.dll, rawpage_en.qm and every dotted path in the tree as a missing
translation. Anchoring on the declared families is what makes it precise enough to fail a
build on.
`command` JOINED AT Stage 3 T5 (plan D3-10 put it at T10): `core/cmd/Command::name()` returns a
`command.*` key from the first command onward, and a family added only when the undo menu shows
it would leave five stages of references unchecked in the meantime.
A reference ENDING IN A DOT is a namespace and is skipped by both rules: several families are
built from a table at runtime -- one key per KeyContext, per settings path, per log subsystem --
so the whole key appears in no source and only the prefix does (T14, issue I-27).
`panes` JOINED AT Stage 4 T5 (plan `Stage4-ViewingSurface-Plan.md` §4), with the first
`ui/panes/` widget that is a view of a DOCUMENT. It is added because the NAMESPACE is new, not
because a feature is -- Stage 3's I-16 is the record of the other reading, where a case required
a `recovery` family for strings that shipped, correctly, as `shell.recovery.*`. The pane's own
chrome inside the sidebar stays `shell.sidebar.*` for the same reason.
Adding a family here is how a new catalog namespace becomes enforced. Leaving one out is a
silent gap, which is why the list is short and why it lives beside scannedPaths rather than in
the tool.
`compare` JOINED AT Stage 5 T13 (`Stage5-TextSearch-Plan.md` D5-20), with its first keys: the
comparison's dialog, view and Differences pane. A new namespace, as `search` was at T7.
`comments` JOINED AT Stage 6 T9 (`Stage6-Annotations-Plan.md` D6-12), with the Comments pane's words. Its
plural is not the action ids' singular -- `comment.reply` is an ActionId, never a key -- so the family
reads no action id as a missing key (Stage 5's I-08). Its pane title stays `panes.comments.title`.
`stamps` JOINED AT Stage 6 T10 (`Stage6-Annotations-Plan.md` D6-16), with the stamp palette's and the
custom-stamp dialog's words and each built-in stamp's name (`stamps.name.`). The action ids stay
`annot.stamp` and `annot.customStamp`, which no `stamps.` key can be mistaken for.
`attachments` JOINED AT Stage 6 T11 (`Stage6-Annotations-Plan.md` D6-17), with the Attachments pane's words and
its questions. Its plural is not the action ids' singular -- `attachment.open` is an ActionId, and
`attachment.add` a command's type id, never a key -- and the pane's title stays `panes.attachments.title`.
$comment-scannedPaths: pdf/ and platform/ were added at Stage 2 T2, and their absence was the same omission twice.
Both layers RETURN Result errors carrying catalog keys -- platform/win/ names eleven of them
and pdf/render/PdfiumInit names the first engine one -- so both reference the catalog exactly
the way core/ does. The absence had no visible effect while pdf/ held one placeholder
translation unit, and the first key added to the engine layer produced a false `orphan-key`
note the same afternoon: the key was referenced, by a file the gate had never been told to
read. That is convention 8 in CLAUDE.md -- a gate reads the files that reference a key, and
whether the gate has been pointed at their directory is a fact about this file rather than
Adding them changes what the LITERAL rule covers as well, which is the half that matters going
forward: pdf/cos/ produces a named error for every malformation it survives, from T5 onward.
It did NOT close the gap issue I-04 records -- `keyFamilies` above and the unknown-key rule did,
at T16. Scanning more directories never finds a key nobody defines; a rule does.
$comment-scanned: core/ is scanned even though it has no tr() and no QObject. That is the point: core/ must hold
no user-facing English at all (core/Result.h says so in its own header comment), so ANY sink
call appearing there is itself the finding rather than a candidate for a tr() wrap.
pdf/ and platform/ are NOT scanned. Neither may put text in front of a user -- pdf/ emits bytes
and platform/ makes no policy decisions -- so a sink call there is a layering violation, which
is layer-lint's job and not a second, weaker copy of it here.
CONSOLE DIAGNOSTICS ARE DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE. app/main.cpp's --version and
--print-dpi-awareness output is developer-facing diagnostic text with a stable, greppable
spelling; translating it would make a support transcript untranslatable back. The CLI's
user-facing surface arrives at Stage 14 and brings its own sinks with it.
$comment-sinks: Each is written with its opening parenthesis so that a MENTION of the name in prose or in an
identifier does not match. setObjectName is deliberately ABSENT: an object name is an internal
identifier that must never be translated, and it is the negative control guide case A-13
warning/critical/information/question are QMessageBox's statics. They are matched bare rather
than as QMessageBox::warning because the idiomatic call sites spell them both ways, and the
cost of the looser match is a literal in some other warning() being reported -- a false
positive, which is visible and waivable, rather than a missed translation.
$comment-escape: unwrapped-literal is a HEURISTIC and is therefore the only escapable rule, using the same
--explain censuses every waiver and says which ones actually SILENCED something. That
distinction is Stage 0's I-20 transplanted before it can happen again: layer-lint once counted
its own documentation as three live waivers, and a census that includes prose cannot do the one
job a census has, which is to show waivers creeping from a handful to a hundred.
